# `pointer-to-allocator`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports struct fields, and function parameters used only through their members,
typed as a pointer to `std.mem.Allocator` under any alias.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`std.mem.Allocator` is an interface struct that consists of a type-erased
pointer and a vtable pointer (`@sizeOf(std.mem.Allocator) == 16`). It is
designed to be passed and stored by value. Passing a pointer to an allocator
adds an unnecessary level of pointer indirection and prevents callers from
passing allocator instances directly (such as `arena.allocator()`,
`gpa.allocator()`, or `testing.allocator`).

## When it fires

On a container field typed `*std.mem.Allocator` or `*const std.mem.Allocator`,
and on a function parameter of that type whose body only calls methods on it,
reads its fields, or copies its pointee (`allocator.*`). The type may be
spelled through `const` aliases such as `const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;`
or `const mem = @import("std").mem;`; a local type that happens to be named
`Allocator` is not reported.

A parameter is left alone when the pointer itself may matter: when it is
passed on, stored, cast (for example to an allocator's `ctx` pointer), or
assigned through (`slot.* = next`), and in exported or C-calling-convention
functions. Local variables, such as `const self: *Allocator = @ptrCast(ctx)` in
an allocator implementation, are never reported. Concrete allocators (such as
`std.heap.ArenaAllocator`) may be passed by pointer when their lifetime or state
is managed across functions.

The quick fix removes the pointer from the type. It is not applied by
`check --fix`, because callers that pass `&allocator` must change too.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn build(allocator: *std.mem.Allocator) ![]u8 {
    return allocator.alloc(u8, 16);
}
```
